version.changelog: Audit round 3: declare all config paths including ~/.openclaw/.env, replace self-overwrite with clawhub update CLI flow, document token scope requirements

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (managing skills in a GitHub-backed repo) aligns with most of its instructions, but it asks for high-privilege GitHub access and reads other local token stores (~/.openclaw/.env), and it dynamically fetches and loads remote skill definitions — those behaviors increase risk and are disproportionate unless you explicitly intend to grant them.

dimensions.detail: The skill is a GitHub-backed skill manager — requiring git and a GitHub token with repo read/write scope is coherent for cloning, fetching index.json, and pushing updates. However the metadata also requires access to ~/.openclaw/.env (an unrelated token store) which is not obviously necessary for standard repo management and is surprising.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions read global and project config files, attempt to read ~/.openclaw/.env as a fallback token source, clone/pull from the private repo, fetch arbitrary index.json and skill files from GitHub, and can download infra files and commit them into the user's repo. Dynamically loading skill definitions from remote repositories means the agent will execute or act on content authored elsewhere — this grants remote content broad influence over your agent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and only a dependency on the git binary. No downloadable install artifacts were specified, so there is no unexpected binary being installed by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires a GitHub PAT (primary credential) with repo read/write scope — a powerful credential that allows modification of the target repository. In addition, the skill is allowed to read ~/.openclaw/.env as a fallback token source; that file may contain unrelated secrets for the agent platform. Requesting access to another token store increases the blast radius and is disproportionate unless explicitly required and consented to by the user.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (no forced inclusion) and autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default). Combined with dynamic remote loading and a write-capable repo token, this gives the skill the ability to fetch new skill definitions and push changes to the repo when invoked — a powerful capability that merits caution, but is not itself a platform privilege escalation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is functionally consistent with a GitHub-backed "skill cloud", but it requires a high-privilege GitHub token and will read an additional local token store (~/.openclaw/.env). Before installing: (1) only provide a GitHub token scoped as narrowly as possible (prefer a repo-specific or fine-grained token, and avoid org-wide privileges); (2) prefer read-only tokens unless you explicitly need to upload/sync or accept changes to your repo; (3) inspect ~/.anyskill/config.json and the repository contents (index.json and any skills) before allowing the skill to auto-load them — remote skill files can cause your agent to perform arbitrary actions; (4) avoid passing tokens on the command line (the SKILL.md suggests git clone with token in URL, which can leak to shell history/process lists) — use a credential helper or environment-only method; (5) if you must use this skill, run it in an isolated environment and revoke the token when not needed. The skill's source is listed in the SKILL.md (github.com/lanyijianke/AnySkill) but the registry entry's source/homepage is unknown — verify authorship and repository contents before trusting it.
